messages:
eli: Heads-up — onboarding xenon13b-int4: we’ve got a weird tokenization/kv-cache mismatch that only shows up with emoji+sigil sequences (variation selectors). CNN/DailyMail summarization scores drop ~4 ROUGE on int4 but not fp16. Repro below.

nina: Can you paste the minimal repro and any token dumps? sounds like a tokenizer-normalization delta. :eyes:

eli: Repro (local):
```python
# encode before conversion
text = 'Breaking: new policy 👩‍⚖️ released'
print(tokenizer.encode(text))
# after conversion step (model file conversion/quant step)
print(tokenizer_converted.encode(text))
```
Observed: first encode -> [131, 4021, 9999, 502]
Converted encode -> [131, 4021, 9999, 503]  # last id off-by-one -> kv alignment shifts.
Also saw a variant where the FE0F (variation selector) becomes its own token in converted tokenizer.

aj: That smells like a normalization/byte-level mapping change during your conversion pipeline. Two likely spots: (1) our tokenizer preproc uses NFKC upstream but the converter uses NFC, or (2) variation selector U+FE0F gets isolated if the unicode normalization step is skipped. The kv cache then indexes by token id so everything downstream shifts.

sam: Ran quant smoke: xenon13b-int4 on summarization canary (10 traces) -> 3 failures where prefix alignment diverges after token 12. Logs show same logits until token 12 then divergence. That matches a token boundary insertion.

ashley: Quick mitigation options:
- Pre-normalize inputs at the API layer: unicode.normalize('NFKC') + strip variation selectors regex.
- Add tokenizer unit test for emoji+zwj sequences to catch regressions.
- Add a conversion-time assert that tokenization of a canonical test-corpus is identical before/after conversion.

deploy-bot: Canary run xenon13b-int4 (canary-2026-03-21) completed: 7/10 traces OK, 3/10 regressed. See dashboard: https://console/redwood/canaries/xenon13b-int4/4968001234 :rotating_light:

eli: For the immediate triage I propose:
1) API pre-normalize inputs for xenon customers (toggleable flag).
2) Add conversion assert (token equality on 100 canonical examples incl emoji/ZWJ).
3) Start a bisect on the conversion toolchain to find when FE0F started tokenizing separately.

nina: Who picks this up? We should also run a quick quant rerun with xenon13b-lite (fp16->int8) to narrow if quant rounding interacts with tokenization. If it's pure tokenization the quant variant should show same token ids mismatch but maybe different downstream severity.

eli: I’ll own the conversion assert + PR. Draft commit msg: "conversion: ensure tokenizer parity post-conversion; add emoji/ZWJ canonical tests; fail fast on token id deltas". I’ll also add a one-liner pre-normalize in the API route as a short-term toggle.

aj: Add an eval job: run rouge/funnel-smoke on 500 examples with and without pre-normalize toggle, capture token-id diffs and kv-cache mismatches. If A/B shows rollback reduces regressions we ship toggle.

eli: Will open PR and link canary results. tagging @nina for review on the eval design. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
